clue.text: Leading men in Enterprise, perhaps

parts.note: leading men in films are the stars
in, meaning fashionable, is hip

explanation.surface: The top executives at a company called Enterprise, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enterprise' poses as a business, but the definition points to the Starship Enterprise of Star Trek; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Enterprise is the famous spacecraft of the Star Trek series, an example of a space vessel.

clue.text: Provide drink then fold

parts.note: to sup is to drink, in small mouthfuls
a ply is a fold or layer, as in two-ply

explanation.surface: Someone serves a drink and then gives up the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fold' suggests a poker player quitting, but it gives PLY, a layer of material.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide something is to furnish or deliver it, the verb sense of the word.

clue.text: I have to follow law that is in force

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first, so it is said to follow it

parts.note: an act is a law passed by Parliament
I have contracts to I've, with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone must obey whichever law is currently in force.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule that is in force is operative or functioning, which is a common sense of the word.

clue.text: If you have them you might not be able to reach their triggers!

definitions.text: If you have them you might not be able to reach their triggers!

parts.words: If you have them you might not be able to reach their triggers!
parts.note: read as a joke about tiny limbs, not weapons: someone with short arms might be unable to reach a trigger, yet the phrase names handheld guns

explanation.surface: A warning about weapons whose triggers are out of reach.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke reads the phrase as stubby limbs rather than pistols and rifles.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names firearms carried by hand, such as pistols and rifles, playfully reread as short limbs.

clue.text: Porcelain is not broken in mum and dad's place

indicators.note: porcelain that is broken is in pieces, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone protests that the china is intact in their parents' house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges PORCELAINISNOT into a Latin legal phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means acting with the authority of a parent, standing where mother and father would.

clue.text: Notices should be put around the German snakes

indicators.note: the first piece is wrapped around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: notices in a newspaper are adverts, ads
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Signs ought to be placed round the German snakes, perhaps as a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is the viper, Britain's only venomous snake.

clue.text: Refuse doctor initially on board ship

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: SS, for steamship, is the vessel one boards

explanation.surface: A medic turns down the chance to go on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is waste matter or rubbish, so it means refuse as a noun.

clue.text: Widespread record I had on electronic microphone

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I had contracts to I'd
mic is short for microphone

explanation.surface: A recording session in which someone used an electronic microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic disease spreads widely through a community, so the adjective means rampant or prevalent.

clue.text: It is insane to clean

indicators.note: the word insane is split, so in tells us the first two words go inside the remainder

parts.note: taken as written, split off from insane

explanation.surface: Someone declares that cleaning is madness.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'insane' into 'in' and 'sane': ITIS goes inside SANE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanitise is to make hygienic by disinfecting, so it means to clean.

clue.text: Scouting revival is all about study

indicators.note: the revival word surrounds the study word on every side

parts.note: a renaissance is a rebirth or revival
to con is to study or learn, an old sense

explanation.surface: A claim that a revival of the Scout movement is entirely about learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconnaissance is military scouting, exploring an area to gather information.

clue.text: Tablet swallowing fat treatment is a danger

indicators.note: the pill takes the other letters inside it, as if swallowed

parts.note: a tablet is a pill

indicators.note: treatment reworks the letters of fat into a new order

explanation.surface: Taking a diet pill to treat fat is risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges FAT to TFA, which goes inside PILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden hazard or trap, so it means a danger.

clue.text: A schoolboy turned to Annie

indicators.note: turned means the letters are churned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A schoolboy turned to a girl named Annie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges TOANNIE; the definition is a pupil at Eton College, a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil at Eton College, the English public school, is a schoolboy of a particular kind.

clue.text: Demolish flat

definitions.meaning: to raze a building to the ground

explanation.definitionFit: To level a building is to raze it, and level ground is smooth and even.

clue.text: The main viewpoint

parts.note: read main as the sea, not chief: a lookout perch high on a ship's mast

explanation.surface: Seems to describe the chief opinion or perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is an old word for the open sea, so this is a sailor's lookout rather than a principal opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: The lookout platform at a ship's masthead is the place from which sailors view the sea.

clue.text: Tendencies for writers to have sex appeal that is starting to shock

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
pens are writing implements
it is old slang for sex appeal
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: starting to says take only the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Authors in favour of sex appeal lean towards the shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: A propensity is an inclination or natural leaning, so the plural means tendencies.

clue.text: The Reverend Robert Walker, for example, is at creek bend

definitions.text: The Reverend Robert Walker, for example

indicators.note: bend means the letters are twisted out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman is pictured at a bend in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Walker is the subject of Raeburn's painting known as The Skating Minister, shown gliding on a frozen loch; 'bend' rearranges ISATCREEK.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reverend Robert Walker is famously painted skating on Duddingston Loch, an example of someone gliding on ice.

clue.text: Table is placed under the trophy cabinet

indicators.note: in a down entry, the board piece is set beneath the cup piece

parts.note: a cup is a trophy
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A table sits below the cabinet holding the trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard is a storage cabinet with doors and shelves.

clue.text: Aussie snappers catch union leader with first pair of secretary's bloomers

indicators.note: the crocodiles enclose the other letters, as if catching them

parts.note: crocs is Australian slang for crocodiles, which snap their jaws

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of union
first pair of means the opening two letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Australian crocodiles grab a union boss along with the secretary's underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocuses are spring flowers, and flowers are bloomers in crossword language.

clue.text: Nurse, badly educated, is out of control

indicators.note: badly signals the preceding word is jumbled into a new order

parts.note: educated means trained

explanation.surface: A poorly educated nurse is running amok.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained means unchecked or uncontrolled, so it fits out of control.

clue.text: Shakespeare is pronounced to be forbidden

indicators.note: is pronounced says the word for Shakespeare is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: Shakespeare is known as the Bard

explanation.surface: Shakespeare is declared banned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something barred is banned or prohibited, so it means forbidden.

clue.text: A boot to fit one easily at first

parts.note: fit, meaning healthy, is well
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A boot that slips on easily.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellie, short for wellington, is a rubber boot.

clue.text: With finance, doctor can construct vertebrae

parts.note: to back a venture is to finance it
bones, from sawbones, is slang for a doctor

explanation.surface: With funding, a physician could build a spinal column.
explanation.definitionFit: The vertebrae make up the spinal column, so the plural fits.

clue.text: Annoy with the French horn

parts.note: to bug is to annoy
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated by the French horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French horn' reads as one instrument, but 'French' belongs with 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle is a brass instrument, a kind of horn.

clue.text: A rogue king went before main body of the church

indicators.note: the king piece is placed in front of the church piece

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
the nave is the central part of a church

explanation.surface: A villainous monarch arrived at the nave ahead of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The knave is also the jack in playing cards, next to the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a dishonest man, a scoundrel or rogue.

clue.text: When one takes a long time returning spear

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as it happened'

indicators.note: returning means this word is read backwards

parts.note: ages means a long time
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone takes ages to bring back a spear.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender spear used by peoples of southern Africa.

clue.text: Ancient city in old South African province is unaffected

indicators.note: in puts the city inside the province

parts.note: Natal was a South African province, now KwaZulu-Natal
Ur is an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An ancient city found within a former South African province remains unspoilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural manner is unaffected, free of pretence or artifice.

clue.text: Ran from father occupied by feminine subject

indicators.note: the father word is filled by the pronoun inside it

parts.note: dad is father
she is the feminine subject pronoun

explanation.surface: A feminine subject fled from their father.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashed means hurried or rushed, past tense, so it matches ran.

clue.text: Resent having to plead before Barnaby

indicators.note: before places the pleading word ahead of the surname

parts.note: to beg is to plead
Barnaby Rudge is a Dickens novel and its title character

explanation.surface: Someone resents having to plead with a man called Barnaby.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Charles Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge is to envy or feel aggrieved, so it fits resent.
